target.title: fix(web-fetch): case-distinct URLs return the wrong cached page
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users fetching two URLs that differ only by letter case could receive the first page's cached response for the second URL. URL paths and query values can be case-sensitive, so lowercasing the whole cache key can return content for a different request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared web cache helper now trims only surrounding whitespace and preserves the case of request-specific key components. This fixes the invariant once for core `web_fetch` and provider-owned web caches without changing cache TTLs, capacity, networking, provider routing, or configuration.

## User Impact

Repeated web fetches and searches no longer share cached content when their request URLs, query values, models, or other case-sensitive dimensions differ only by case.

## Evidence

- Live third-party proof with Postman Echo through the repository's OpenClaw `createOpenClawTools()` -> `web_fetch` production path:
  - Before: requesting `marker=openclawcase` after `marker=OpenClawCase` returned `OpenClawCase` with `cached: true`.
  - Control: independent Postman Echo requests returned `OpenClawCase` and `openclawcase` respectively.
  - After: both OpenClaw requests returned their requested value and the second request was not an incorrect cache hit.
- Red/green regression: the new test failed on current main because both cache keys normalized to lowercase, then passed after the fix.
- `pnpm test src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-tools.fetch.test.ts src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.test.ts` — 49 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:prod` — passed for core, UI, and extensions.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — no actionable findings.
- `pnpm build` was attempted; the `openclaw-unified` bundler process was terminated by SIGTERM after 97 seconds without a source diagnostic, so the full local build did not complete.
